summary: Codenames: Duet is a two-player cooperative twist on Codenames where both players are spymasters and guessers simultaneously, working together to find all 15 agents within a limited number of turns before hitting an assassin. It keeps the same word-clueing tension but reframes it as a shared puzzle rather than a competition.
praised: Same clever wordplay tension as the original, now collaborative
Turn limit creates real pressure and stakes
Great for couples or small groups wanting co-op
criticised: Loses the competitive team-vs-team energy of the original
Can feel frustrating when communication styles clash
Fixed turn limit sometimes feels too harsh

interaction.detail: Both players alternate giving clues to each other over the same shared grid, and each player's assassin squares differ from the other's key card, so misjudging a clue can cost the whole team a turn or the game. The board and win/loss state are entirely shared between the two players.

scoring.why: Both players win or lose together based solely on whether all green agent cards are found before time or guesses run out or the assassin is hit.
scoring.how_you_win: Working from different keycards, both players give and interpret clues together to identify all 15 shared agent words within a limited number of turns/guesses, without touching an assassin word.
